I will never take any animal there again, nor would I recommend it to anyone.
We went there for an emergency, and a girl who didn't know what she was doing attended to us. It was a complete disaster, and my dog ​​suffered the consequences.

If you're reading reviews because you have doubts, don't go! I didn't read any reviews because an acquaintance recommended it, and we had an urgent injury. But the recent reviews are terrible. There must be a reason. It's a shame that a place where the well-being of animals should be paramount doesn't prioritize them.

Extremely expensive, never going back. €711
for an emergency.
The dog was fine a few hours later without having received the treatment.
We took our dog in because she wasn't moving, and the day before we saw her with something in the trash. They did an x-ray and blood work because they thought she might have a foreign object. I asked why not do an ultrasound, and the vet said the ultrasound technician wasn't available.
Up to this point, they told me it would cost around €400.
Then they said the blood work was fine, but there was a spot on the x-ray, and that we needed to do an ultrasound, another €219.
An hour later, they called me back and said the ultrasound showed she had a lot of gas. I asked about the foreign object, and they said it wasn't important and that she would pass it.
They gave me a probiotic treatment, an anti-vomiting medication, and a complementary food.
In short, €711. They scare you with the x-ray, only to tell you after the ultrasound that it's just gas. I was the one who suffered from feeling manipulated. My vet charges less than €100 for an ultrasound, visit, and treatment.

Bittersweet experience:
First of all, I should mention that this hospital was recommended to me a few weeks ago. Our dog swallowed a whole chicken bone one night, and we had to go there at 11:00 PM. When we arrived, the receptionist was very kind; she triaged him, took his vital signs, and so on. Then we went to the examination room, and the veterinarian explained the situation. An endoscopy would be necessary, and surgery would be required if the bone couldn't be removed. So far, so good. The problem was that while explaining this, she wouldn't look us in the eye, and the second thing she mentioned was the price, the money, and the bills. We were facing a possible operation for our 8-month-old puppy, and what we felt most was that they were only concerned with the financial aspect. After admitting him, we had to go outside to pay. We paid in advance for the endoscopy and the possible stomach surgery (€2163), which I thought was terrible. Without even knowing if the procedure was necessary, they made us pay upfront, and the prices are exorbitant (€537 for the emergency supplement, €906 for the operation, €500-something for the endoscopy...) It's insane! They told us they would call us back with the news, that it would take about an hour, so we stalled and went back an hour later to ask. Another receptionist told us the dog was already under anesthesia but they were waiting for the vet to arrive at the clinic, which also seemed surreal to us since if it's an emergency, we don't understand how the vet has to come from home... After several hours, they finally called to say they had removed the bone endoscopically, so in that respect, they did a great job. The dog walked out on his own and we were able to leave. It's worth noting that they couldn't refund us for the operation they didn't perform immediately; we had to go back the next day to swipe our card in person. And I should also mention that during our stay we noticed some things that didn't add up, like the vets not communicating with each other, they lost our leash (which they later found), and they got confused about the procedures... Based on my experience, I wouldn't go back unless it was a VERY URGENT case, but I definitely would NOT recommend it.

Yesterday I was in with my dog ​​because he had a black eye, even though we weren't aware he'd hit it. They kept us waiting for two and a half hours because there were so many patients, and when it was finally our turn, they took the dog into the examination room and then came out a little while later telling us they didn't have any ophthalmology emergencies. And they charged us €45 for "triage." Unbelievable. Draw your own conclusions.

Thank you so much, AnitaXVII, for your 5 stars! 🥰 That means you had a wonderful experience at Veterios Reference Veterinary Hospital and took the time to let us know.

We trust we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet.

Have a great day, and see you soon!

I clearly specified that I needed everything resolved in one visit for the animal's health. Instead of telling me they couldn't handle it and that I should find another clinic, I only found out 7 hours before the appointment because I thought to call that it wasn't possible, even though they initially told me it could be done without a problem. I already have another clinic that, when I explain the problem, resolves everything in one visit. Zero professionalism and zero personalization of cases; they'll do anything to make a little more money. Otherwise, I can't find any explanation; everyone can draw their own conclusions. I won't be going back here.
They saved little Lya's life, we will be forever grateful. Thank you for your work ❤️
I took my dog ​​to an emergency vet at night. The vet explained the tests they had done and gave us some guidelines. Very professional. The place is welcoming and clean. Highly recommended.

I want to sincerely thank Inés, the veterinarian at Veterios, for her professionalism, dedication, and above all, for accurately diagnosing our dog, Mia.

We were very worried and filled with uncertainty, but Inés was able to assess her condition, ask the right questions, and arrive at the diagnosis of meningitis. It was a very difficult time for us, and having a professional who could identify what was happening to Mia gave us a great deal of peace of mind and confidence.

We are incredibly grateful for her care, for how she explained the situation to us, and for the love with which she treated our little one. It's clear when a veterinarian not only has knowledge but also a true calling and empathy for animals and their families.

Thank you, Inés, for helping Mia and for being there for us during such a distressing time. We will always be very grateful.

Many thanks to the Veterios team, we were able to save this baby (Duna) whom we rescued from a colony near our home. At just a few months old, she was extremely malnourished and very sick; the prognosis was uncertain, but the hospital staff did everything they could during her stay, and we succeeded. Now she's growing strong and happy, gaining weight every day.

The hospital service is very well organized, the facilities are in good condition (there's parking inside and you can also park nearby); the care is quite efficient. Keep in mind that it's an emergency center, and sometimes you have to wait in order of arrival, but the staff coordinates well, weighing the severity of each case based on their professional experience, as is only natural. As for the treatments, they were started without delay, and all the necessary tests were performed. We didn't waste time with half-baked "diagnoses" or one test after another while the animal got worse, without getting anywhere (as happened to me in the past at another clinic). DISCLAIMER: Every pet is unique and each case is independent, and based on this, a different protocol is followed. This review is our specific experience. In conclusion, 100% recommended.

My dog ​​was referred there because he needed an urgent ultrasound, and unfortunately, I encountered a group of completely unsympathetic veterinarians who were only interested in exploiting the emotions and desperation of pet owners to perform more tests than necessary and charge more money.

It's very sad to encounter people who lack vocation and are only interested in money.
They tried to keep my dog ​​hospitalized, but I refused. Fortunately, with the treatment prescribed by his longtime veterinarian, my dog ​​is doing well.
I do not recommend this place, and it's very sad to encounter these kinds of people.

Thank you so much, Cristina, for your review! We're delighted to hear you were happy with our service after your visit.
We trust we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet.
Have a great day,
Veterinos Referral Veterinary Hospital
We took my kitten there, and not only were we treated very well, but they also saved his life. Accurate diagnosis. Highly recommended.

Thank you so much, Msk, for your review! We're delighted to hear you were happy with our service after your visit.
We trust we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet.
Have a great day,
Veterinos Referral Veterinary Hospital

On July 8th, we rushed him to this hospital after being referred from the Atocha emergency room, where we usually take him. The dog wasn't eating and had lost strength in his hind legs, and this was starting to happen in his front legs as well. In addition, the dog had been suffering for several months from emphysematous cystitis resistant to practically all antibiotics. When we admitted him, we said we thought the lack of appetite and weakness could be due to the antibiotic he was taking, since the side effects matched what was listed in the package insert and coincided with the onset of the symptoms. Even so, they ignored us and said they didn't think that was the cause. They started running a bunch of neurological tests (which cost us a fortune) before finally taking him off the antibiotic. And lo and behold! After stopping it, the dog coincidentally began to improve.

Regarding the cystitis, we've only received one call from internal medicine, and they charged us for a consultation to tell us absolutely nothing. We already knew everything they said on the call: to leave the dog without antibiotics and wait for a culture and antibiogram. It's been 15 days now, and we still haven't received any response from anyone in internal medicine. The dog's cystitis is getting worse again, and no matter how much I ask for information, nobody here is calling. After the first ultrasound of his bladder, a veterinarian called me and painted a very grim picture, saying that these cases of cystitis have a terrible prognosis… but nobody here is doing anything. It seems like they're waiting for the infection to spread to his kidneys and for the dog to die. I also don't know which lab they use that takes so long to give us results.

But the administrative side is a disaster too. Every single time I had to request the dog's insurance form, filled out by the vet, because they'd had it for five or six days and no one was sending anything. They just leave it there in a pile, and if you don't insist... in short, zero peace of mind.

It's an extremely expensive hospital (compared to other emergency centers I've been to) that they advertise as a "reference" center, but I don't know exactly what that means, given what I've seen.

Reply to your response: No, my complaint isn't based on worry or frustration, but on the incompetence, lack of humanity, and lack of professionalism of the staff at this hospital.

It's not that I think they should have tried stopping the antibiotic sooner (because it was obvious), his regular vet also said so several times, but they didn't even bother to talk to him... It's normal that the dog didn't improve 12 hours after stopping it; he'd been on it for 10 days. The body has to eliminate the remaining medication (it won't do that in 12 hours; a vet should know that).

After the complaint, surprisingly, the culture results were already in (what a coincidence!), and they prescribed three injections of Convenia every 15 days for the infection. Well, he's already had the three injections. Did they tell me to repeat the culture? No. I told the vet, Miriam, who again isn't responding (I have the email I sent her; no reply and not even a call). Luckily, I'm much more competent than they are, and before the effect of her last dose wore off, I already had an appointment with her regular vet, who repeated the culture, and we're waiting for the results. (I highly recommend Alonso Cano Veterinary Clinic.)

I filed a complaint, and it seems the coordinator has better things to do than deal with dissatisfied customers because he never bothered to contact me.

In short: you and your animals mean absolutely nothing to them; they have zero dedication and just want your money. Seriously, there are much better places in Madrid (it's not hard to find).
Excellent and very quick service for an emergency we had with our cat, but we felt the price was excessive; nowadays, having pets has become a luxury.

Our experience with the Veterios Veterinary Hospital (which was anything but a referral clinic) was solely BY PHONE, because we couldn't even get them to see our dog.
We called in complete desperation. Our dog was 15 years old, terminally ill, in a lot of pain, and had already been scheduled for euthanasia on Monday afternoon at another clinic.
We weren't calling looking for miracles. We didn't want to subject an elderly, terminally ill dog to more and more tests. We were calling looking for something much simpler and more humane: for them to see our dog urgently and alleviate his suffering.
We explained the situation and that we had all the tests and analyses that his veterinary clinic had already performed and that we could provide them.
We just wanted someone to listen and understand the situation: WE HAD A 15-YEAR-OLD DOG, TERMINALLY ILL AND IN PAIN. We were a desperate family trying to end our dog's suffering so we could say a dignified goodbye.

We weren't asking to be saved. We weren't looking for a miracle cure. We didn't want to unnecessarily prolong an irreversible situation.
WE WERE ASKING FOR HELP SO OUR DOG WOULDN'T SUFFER.

And we couldn't even get him to be seen.

In a situation like this, it's impossible not to ask: where does animal welfare fit in?

For us, animal welfare isn't just about diagnosing, testing, or administering treatments. It also means having empathy, understanding when an animal is at the end of its life, and helping a desperate family avoid unnecessary suffering.
The feeling we were left with after that call was one of helplessness, anger, and a profound lack of humanity during one of the most painful moments a family can experience with their dog.

Our dog was suffering. We were desperate. We were only looking for help to alleviate his pain.

And we couldn't even get him to be seen.

A deeply disappointing and painful phone experience.
One star because I can't give zero.
They are good professionals but, like all emergency services, they seem too distant with the animals.

To be honest, my husband and I were initially very worried after reading so many bad reviews, especially after choosing this clinic and already being there with Simba, our cat. We had to go to the emergency room because Simba had swallowed an office rubber band and wouldn't stop vomiting, wasn't eating, was lethargic, and wasn't going to the bathroom. Alejandro, the emergency veterinarian, saw us, explained everything he considered important for Simba, and showed us the ultrasound and X-rays they had taken as an emergency. He told us his recommendation was to keep him hospitalized and that if he passed the foreign object that night, surgery wouldn't be necessary. I wasn't worried about the cost, although that's important too; I was more afraid of the surgery and the recovery. Alejandro answered all our questions about the possible scenarios and also explained what to do afterward if Simba needed surgery the next morning. He was equally transparent with us about the cost. He was patient and caring.

Everything done in the emergency room was charged accordingly, but everything they did for the kitten once he was admitted wasn't overpriced at all, from our point of view. This is something we'd read a lot in reviews, and it was another thing that scared us when we arrived and were inside the hospital. We didn't know what to expect, but it was quite the opposite.

The next day, Julia, who was in the hospitalization ward, called us to reassure us that he was better and the foreign object had passed into his colon. She recommended that Simba stay at the hospital for 24 hours so they could observe him, keep him hydrated, and then we could pick him up. We did as she said. She also called me later to explain the report, the medication, and how to proceed in the coming days, and to tell me again that Simba was doing well.

We went to pick up Simba at night and had to put him in the carrier ourselves because he didn't want anything to do with anyone anymore, but he reacted very happily to us and we took him home. I loved how clean everything was and the spaces where they kept all the kittens were quite spacious and comfortable for them. I'm sure the dog area was just as good.
Simba continues to improve after being well cared for and receiving excellent advice. We want to thank Alejandro, Julia, and all the staff who helped us for their patience and attention. Of course, we'll be back, and this time without fear, in case we have any further problems, which we hope will be a long time from now. Have a good day. Don't be swayed by the reviews; our experience was truly positive in every way.

I took my dog ​​there this week and I have nothing but praise for this clinic. The reception staff were wonderful, as was the veterinarian who treated us (Alberto). Impeccable and highly professional service. I would definitely recommend it.

Thank you, Olga, for your 5 stars! We're so glad to hear you had a positive experience at Veterios Referral Veterinary Hospital. ❤ We'd love to make your experience even better on your next visit. Is there anything you'd recommend we improve?

Thank you so much, Cecilia, for your 5 stars! 🥰 That means you had a wonderful experience at Veterios Reference Veterinary Hospital and took the time to let us know.

We trust we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet.

Have a great day, and see you soon!

Ana, we're saddened to hear you had a negative experience at Veterios Referral Veterinary Hospital. 💔 Our center is known for its excellence, dedication, and care for pets, as evidenced by the positive reviews from many clients. Please tell us in detail what happened. …

Our experience at Clínica Veteros was very negative, and frankly, we felt more like customers who needed to be charged than like people who had brought our dog in seeking a solution.

In June, we went with our dog, bringing a report that already stated she had a hernia and that the problem was related to pain. Even so, they recommended an MRI, which cost €1,200. We believe that, having this information and prior diagnosis, they should have explained much better the real need for such an expensive test and whether it would actually provide any different results.
What bothered us most was that when we returned a few days later to check on our dog, they charged us for the consultation again.
We are left with the feeling that tests were performed and expenses incurred that, from our point of view, were unnecessary, instead of prioritizing veterinary care focused on the animal's well-being and the actual needs of the case. We fully understand that a veterinary clinic needs to charge for its services and that certain tests may be necessary, but in our case, the experience left us very disappointed and with the feeling that the financial aspect played too large a role.
Based on our experience, we will not return and cannot recommend this clinic.

My experience with this veterinary clinic on August 18, 2026, was terrible. If I could give it zero stars, I would. We went in at 12:30 AM and left at 10:30 PM WITHOUT ANY DIAGNOSIS. This clinic should be closed. THEY ARE NOT HUMANE; they don't care at all about the animal's health.

I took my cat in because he had a small wound and a lump on his chin, and they referred me to this clinic. From the first moment, I had the feeling that they prioritized running test after test instead of going directly to the test that could actually clarify what was wrong with my cat: a biopsy.

As soon as we arrived, they performed blood work, X-rays, and then a cytology. To get the sample, they had to prick him three times: the first time it wasn't valid, the second time wasn't either, and finally, they had to prick him a third time, this time sedating him. Watching my cat go through all of this only to not get the diagnosis we needed was heartbreaking.

Furthermore, they mentioned the possibility of metastasis and suggested further tests and the possibility of hospitalizing him. I later consulted another veterinarian for a second opinion, and the situation they explained was completely different: no metastasis was detected, and they indicated that, in his case, a biopsy was the necessary test to correctly determine what was happening in his jaw.

What infuriates me most is that this biopsy could have been considered from the beginning, and yet my cat underwent several tests, three injections, and sedation without us ever getting a definitive diagnosis.

I also find it particularly concerning that they suggested hospitalizing him, when another professional later explained that this type of biopsy doesn't necessarily mean the animal needs to be admitted.

After this experience, my feeling is that they prioritized running tests and increasing the bill over finding the most direct and appropriate procedure to diagnose my cat. I spent money, watched my pet endure completely unnecessary stress, and ended up having to go to another veterinarian for a second opinion and further diagnosis.

When we take a sick animal to a veterinary clinic, we are in a state of immense worry and vulnerability, and we trust that every test performed is truly necessary. I didn't feel that trust at any point.

I do not recommend this clinic. My experience on August 18, 2026, was very negative, both because of the way the case was handled and because of the number of tests performed without arriving at the diagnosis we needed. I certainly would not take any of my animals there again.

Experience with Veterios
Our experience with the Veterios Veterinary Hospital has been absolutely devastating, and after what happened, we cannot recommend this center.

Last Sunday, around 11:30 p.m., we took our cat Blane to the clinic. He was in very serious condition. He had three gallstones, one of them in the bile duct, and had been diagnosed with triaditis. There was also a possibility that his gallbladder had perforated. We offered them the report from his regular veterinarian, but they refused to accept it.
The following morning, they informed us that Blane had eaten a Churu (a type of cat food) and that they needed to perform abdominal punctures. I specifically asked if they had performed an ultrasound and if they had seen the stones. They assured me twice that there were no stones, even though I insisted that he had three and explained exactly where they were.
Concerned, we contacted his regular veterinarian, who told us to request a voluntary discharge and take him to her clinic immediately.

Upon reviewing the Veterios documentation, we found that the blood test was recorded at 00:30 and the ultrasound at 09:07. We still don't know what happened to our pet during those hours, despite having expressly requested this information in writing on two occasions.
At her usual veterinarian, a new ultrasound was performed, confirming that the gallbladder had perforated and that the stones were present. Even when we showed her the Veterios images, she pointed to one of the stones and asked how they could have told us there weren't any.
Blane was in great pain, and we ultimately had to make the decision to euthanize her to avoid prolonging her suffering.
Later, we asked to speak with a manager to get an explanation. Instead of answering our questions about what happened to our pet, we were repeatedly told about protocols and the company. We were even told that it was normal to look for someone to hold accountable during our grief and that we shouldn't forget that we had chosen that hospital. In our opinion, this response was completely inappropriate.

Blane was in great pain, and we finally had to make the decision to euthanize her to avoid prolonging her suffering. We do not dispute that Blane's condition was very serious, nor that the outcome was inevitable. What we do question are the contradictions, the lack of information, and the fact that, after requesting it twice, we still haven't received a complete timeline of what happened.
This very painful experience and lack of transparency prevent us from recommending this center.

A complete nightmare.

Eva

Our experience at Veterios was absolutely disappointing and, unfortunately, ended with the loss of our cat, Blane.
We arrived with a very sick animal, with a known history of illness and in pain. The care we received was extremely cold and distant: they took our cat away and we barely had any contact with him for many hours. Furthermore, the paperwork included procedures such as a biopsy and CPR that we had neither discussed nor authorized. Nasogastric feeding was also initially indicated, and we had to specifically request that it be removed.
The most serious thing for us was that, when we decided it was time to let him go to prevent further suffering, they initially refused to perform euthanasia because the veterinarian didn't feel comfortable doing it. They told us he had eaten and was lively, despite his serious decline and months of illness and increasingly severe relapses.

We requested a voluntary discharge and, after a very long wait, Blane was returned to us. We then took him to his usual veterinarian, who, upon seeing him, noticed obvious jaundice, reviewed his blood work, and performed an ultrasound. The ultrasound showed that his gallbladder had ruptured and that the gallstones we already knew about were still there. We finally decided to let him go.

The difference in the treatment was enormous. His veterinarian treated us with humanity, gentleness, and empathy, allowed us to be with him, and supported us through one of the most painful moments of our lives.

I don't question that a hospital has protocols or charges for its services. I question the lack of communication, the way they proceeded, and, above all, the feeling that our pet's well-being was not their priority.
We will not return to Veterios, and based on our experience, we cannot recommend it. We hope our experience will encourage other families to ask many questions before leaving a sick animal there.

A regrettable experience. On August 14th, since our regular veterinarian was on vacation, we took our 18-year-old cat to the Veterios clinic near Plenilunio. The cat was quite ill; he had barely eaten for days and was constantly defecating throughout the house. After several tests and a rather expensive treatment, we went home, but far from improving, the cat worsened.
Ten days later, on the clinic's first day of operation, we took him to our regular veterinarian. After a manual examination, the vet determined that the cat had a 6 cm tumor in his stomach, a finding later confirmed by an ultrasound. Sadly, we had to euthanize him that same day due to the severity of his condition. I believe in the honesty of the veterinarians at Veterios, but I find it difficult to understand how, after performing several tests and seeing the cat's condition, they failed to notice something that another veterinarian could detect with a simple manual examination. This leads me to suspect that, unfortunately, sometimes business profit takes precedence over honesty.
Today, I went to the clinic to demand an explanation, and the coordinator refused to acknowledge the serious error committed. I hope these cases are not repeated and that the health of our animals and honesty prevail above all else, rather than the desire to make money—something I'm sure all veterinarians worldwide agree with.
Veterinary hospitals aren't cheap, but they save lives. Thank you.

Please DO NOT take your pet here. We brought our cat, Blane, in for emergency care. He had a serious pancreatic condition and a significant medical history, including gallstones that could have worsened at any moment. From the very beginning, we provided all his information and veterinary reports.

Despite it being an emergency, they told us they hadn't been able to medicate him yet because they were "overwhelmed." That night, they only performed blood work, and the ultrasound was done the following day, even though we had informed them of the severity of his condition and his medical history. Furthermore, we feel that the information we provided wasn't listened to or valued as it should have been.

Later, his regular veterinarian confirmed that the stones were clearly visible and that the situation was extremely serious. Blane ultimately passed away.

We knew he was very ill, and we aren't looking for someone to blame or miracles. What hurts us most is thinking that he may have suffered for hours and that perhaps some of that suffering could have been avoided with faster care and by taking into account all the information we provided.

The lack of empathy and humanity we felt throughout the process, both towards us and when trying to get explanations afterward, made the experience even more painful.

I hope no other family has to go through something like this.
Emma is treating my dog ​​Mago in the neurology department. I've had a great experience there; she's very attentive to his case and his progress, and all the staff are very friendly!

I went to the emergency room and Cristina treated me; she was excellent in terms of the clarity of her explanations. The only downside I see is the prices, which are rather exorbitant. They charged me 500 euros, including the emergency room visit, blood tests, X-ray, and stitches.

They have no clue. I took my dog ​​in for what we now know was a lumbar dislocation. Not only did they not examine him properly or run any tests, but they assumed he had a broken toe and told us we needed blood tests and x-rays of that area for no apparent reason. Clearly, 500 euros for nothing. They're only interested in making money and couldn't care less about the well-being and care of the animals.

This hospital and its professionals are a disgrace. We took my cat in because he had an unknown kidney problem. The same day we admitted him, we asked to be kept informed of everything and whether surgery was necessary. The answer was yes. After four days in the hospital and €1500, they discharged him, saying he had a kidney stone and one kidney was slightly larger than the other, without giving him any medication. A month later, another vet performed a CT scan and told us he had a serious kidney infection that had already affected his stomach. They even told us that if he had been operated on while he was hospitalized, the problem could have been resolved. A week later, we had to euthanize my 10-year-old cat because he stopped eating and was drooling blood. We will do everything possible to prevent anyone from ever taking an animal to this center again because you let my cat die, and who knows if you do the same to other people's pets. You bunch of crooks! You shameless people who only want money and not the well-being of the animals.

Well-organized and equipped with state-of-the-art facilities. A wide range of veterinary specialties with highly qualified professionals. Prices are high, but commensurate with the quality and efficiency of the service provided. Ample and convenient on-site parking is available for emergencies.

The facilities are exceptional, but they pale in comparison to the professionalism and care of the staff: doctors, assistants, and reception personnel. I highly recommend Veterios to anyone with a pet who needs emergency care. No matter the distance, your pet will always be in the best hands.

My experience was quite unfortunate, not because of the clinic itself, but because of the first veterinarian who saw me, Andrea. I took my dog ​​there, referred by my usual vet, for an abdominal ultrasound to assess any potential injuries. When they took the dog and returned some time later, the veterinarian told me he was very ill and needed to be admitted. She gave me this information without even having performed the ultrasound we had been referred for. I told her I would decide that once I had the results. My companion left, and that's when this veterinarian took the opportunity to tell me that if I took the dog home and didn't admit him, he could die, and she repeated this twice. I told her I wanted to see the dog, and she said not yet, only after the ultrasound. An hour and a half had already passed with the dog in there and the ultrasound still hadn't been done. I could tell you all about the visit and conversation with this person, but I think this is enough to see how this vet plays with the emotions of pet owners to maximize their bills.
As soon as I got the ultrasound results, I took my little one straight to my usual clinic.
By the way, the ultrasound didn't show anything serious.
The next day, with the care my vet recommended after reviewing the ultrasound report, my puppy was as good as new.

And I repeat, I'm not giving a bad review to the hospital in this case, but to that specific vet.
What I really don't like about the hospital is that they don't let you stay with your pet.

Good hospital and good care, thank you very much.

I have an elderly Alaskan Malamute named Argi with cancer. I am so grateful for all the effort they are putting into treating her. I thank the entire team, especially the oncologist Sergio and the surgeon Manuel, for their great dedication and commitment.

Thank you so much, Margarita, for sharing your positive experience at Veterios Referral Veterinary Hospital! We are confident that we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet on your next visit.
Excellent service, only words of gratitude for the treatment we received along with my cat Figaro, especially thanks to Sergio from oncology.

Thank you so much, Mariajose, for your 5 stars! 🥰 That means you had a wonderful experience at Veterios Reference Veterinary Hospital and took the time to let us know.

We trust we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet.

Have a great day, and see you soon!

The care we received from the entire Veterios team during our dog's treatment was excellent.

Special mention to Dr. Manuel for his outstanding work as a surgeon, and to Dr. Sergio for his kindness and reassuring support throughout Odin's cancer treatment.

In difficult times with our pets, finding such a compassionate and dedicated team makes a world of difference. Thank you to the entire Veterios team for caring for Odin with such love and dedication. Without a doubt, this hospital is highly recommended.

We're taking my Toy Poodle to rehabilitation, and Patricia is lovely. So far, everything is great. My dog ​​is thrilled. The service is outstanding. We couldn't be happier. Thank you so much, Patricia!

To be honest, it leaves much to be desired. I arrived with my dog ​​and found the gate closed. After knocking twice, they finally answered and asked what was wrong with my dog. I told them he'd been vomiting since 4:30 PM and that at 12:50 AM, after vomiting blood, I brought him in. They told me they couldn't help him and that I should go to a vet on the other side of Madrid (Retiro Park).

My experience at this veterinary hospital was not satisfactory. We went because our dog was vomiting and we noticed she was having trouble with her hind legs. Upon arrival, they told us she needed an abdominal x-ray, which cost around €270, which we agreed to because we wanted to know what was wrong.

After about half an hour, they called us in. Among others, we were seen by a neurologist, who explained that our dog had several neurological issues and facial paralysis. They asked if she might have ingested any drugs, such as marijuana, since we mentioned that we had seen her eat something in the street, although we didn't know what it was. They also told us that the x-ray showed nothing, only an empty stomach, and that the next step was to perform blood tests and a brain CT scan, which would cost over €1,000. Furthermore, they mentioned that all the explanations they had given us normally came at a cost, but that on this occasion they were offering them free of charge. At that moment, we felt very uncomfortable and with the sense that the focus was more on proposing very expensive tests than on considering other options.

We decided to go to our usual veterinarian the next day. She confirmed that there was facial paralysis, ran some tests that came back completely normal, and, upon reviewing the same X-ray that had been taken at the hospital, found contents in the stomach that, as she explained, were indeed visible, even though the hospital had assured us there was nothing there. We also had to insist that they send us both the X-rays and the report, which we didn't receive until almost 11 p.m.

Finally, with treatment to help cleanse the liver of the toxin she had likely ingested, although it hasn't been possible to identify which one, our dog has improved significantly. The facial paralysis is gradually subsiding, and she no longer has dizziness or the problems she had at the beginning.

I respect that each professional may have a different opinion, but personally, I left with the feeling that very expensive tests were prioritized without first exhausting other, simpler diagnostic options. Therefore, my experience was not positive, and I believe it's important to share it so that other owners can make their own decision.

The treatment I received, and especially my dog's, was excellent. My sincerest thanks to the cardiology team and all the staff who cared for my dog ​​when I had to take him to the emergency room; thanks to them, he's still by my side.

Today we took Hugo, our cat, in because he had a piece of plastic stuck in his teeth, and they fixed it immediately. Sandra's service was excellent; she was wonderful with him. 100% recommended! Thank you so much!!
Good service

Excellent service from the first moment we contacted them. Pablo explained everything very clearly and sent us the results and treatment recommendations by email so we could discuss them with Oliver's regular veterinarians.
So far, everything is working. Thank you so much for everything. Highly recommended!
The service was spectacular; I hope I never have to take my kitten there again, but if I did, I would definitely take him there.

My recommendation for this clinic is very negative. My experience has been terrible, after more than a year.

After 5 hours and nearly €400 in tests and treatment, they sent my dog ​​home with terrible swelling and pain. The only response we received was that she needed more tests. My feeling was that, unable to find the source of the problem, the only solution they offered was to continue performing tests without providing a clear explanation or a plan of action that would inspire confidence.

What shocked us most was that, when we mentioned we had already spent around €1,000 on tests without a diagnosis and that we didn't want to continue with more tests without a clear rationale or results, the response we received was to suggest euthanasia. Instead of explaining other alternatives or trying to find other ways to reach a diagnosis, they presented us with that option, which left us completely devastated. In our opinion, recommending such an extreme measure when there was still no clear diagnosis and without offering us other solutions was very difficult to understand and accept.

Furthermore, we were later given to understand that we were the ones who didn't want to continue with the tests. This isn't true. What we wanted was for them to explain what they were looking for, what options were available, and what the medical criteria were for each decision, instead of feeling like more tests were simply piling up without answers.

It was the worst treatment I have ever received in my entire life at a veterinary clinic. The helplessness of going there seeking help for your pet and leaving without answers, watching them suffer, is overwhelming.

As the person who treated my dog ​​told me, "If you don't like it, don't come back." Honestly, I think that was the most sensible thing I heard during this whole experience.

Thank you so much Raluca for sharing your positive experience at Veterios Reference Veterinary Hospital! We are confident that we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet on your next visit.

Our beloved Bli passed away on June 27th. From here, I extend my deepest gratitude to the entire hospital team. They did everything possible and more. The exceptional care they gave both my Bli and us was truly admirable.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

I went to the emergency vet on Saturday because my cat was vomiting, had diarrhea, and wasn't eating or drinking. They did blood work and X-rays, sending us home with an explanation of the tests and saying nothing looked wrong, with a possible diagnosis of gastroenteritis or colic. €428 for the whole ordeal, only to leave without knowing for sure what was wrong. The cat remained lethargic, barely eating anything, and I had to give him water with a syringe and some food. I almost took him back the next day for hospitalization, as they had recommended, but thankfully my vet contacted me and kindly came to see what was going on, even though she wasn't open on Sundays. She had received the reports from this clinic and found it strange that there was no diagnosis or prescribed treatment other than pain medication. She was amazed when she saw the X-rays, saying that the amount of gas the cat had and the thickening of the intestinal/colon walls weren't normal and indicated that something was wrong. She couldn't do an ultrasound, but apparently, that would have been the essential step given the case and the symptoms. Even without the X-ray, just with the X-rays, she clearly saw that they could be interpreted based on what they showed (which wasn't that everything was fine and that it was normal for the cat to be like that). She administered various medications, and after 4 hours, the cat was eating and drinking like crazy. Since then, 48 hours ago, the cat hasn't stopped eating or drinking, and the diarrhea is now under control. In short, I absolutely do not recommend going to this place. I went because of a recommendation, as they are known for their humane treatment (which I have no complaints about, because they treated me kindly, and I imagine they treated the cat well too... although I couldn't see him again from the time they admitted him until we left), and because I was terrified to see him so sick and getting worse in the middle of the weekend, but obviously, I wouldn't go back for anything. Aside from the exorbitant cost, the cat wasn't diagnosed even though the tests clearly showed he wasn't well... and we were sent home without a solution, not only leaving him feeling unwell but actually making him worse. The least one could expect, given the price we paid, is a proper diagnosis and treatment tailored to the animal's needs. I felt ripped off and put the animal's health at risk.

IN MY RESPONSE TO THEIR PROVIDEMENT: They claim the x-ray showed no abnormalities that could lead to a diagnosis. However, two other veterinarians DID see that the x-ray clearly showed something abnormal, such as excessive gas accumulation and thickening of the intestinal walls, which you did NOT tell me, nor did you prescribe any treatment. I personally asked the veterinarian to perform an ultrasound if necessary to see what was going on, because according to her, nothing unusual was visible and it could be many things. She told me it wasn't necessary at the moment, just to see how things progressed. They charged me €428 and left without a diagnosis, without treatment, and with my cat's condition worsening. It's shameful how unprofessional and lacking in judgment they are, when they can't even interpret an X-ray that, according to two other professionals, clearly shows an abnormality.

It's a trustworthy veterinary clinic with a very friendly and approachable team. They've always treated us with professionalism and care, making us feel well looked after. As with any place, there are always areas for improvement, but overall, our experience has been very positive, and I would definitely recommend it.
I don't recommend it at all.
3/4 hours waiting for some tests.

We will NOT be returning. We went there urgently on a Saturday because our dog couldn't walk or stand due to neuropathic problems. After waiting three hours in the waiting room (literally), they simply gave him an anti-inflammatory, which is not appropriate for his condition, and didn't offer any kind of diagnosis. They had no idea. To our further surprise and disappointment: the consultation alone costs €140… We were definitely ripped off.

Our experience at Veterios has been bittersweet.

I want to begin by highlighting the professionalism, dedication, and compassionate care of Pablo, head of Internal Medicine, and the professionalism and immense kindness of cardiologist Carlos Fonseca. I also want to express my gratitude for the treatment we received from other members of the staff. That's precisely why I feel it's important to share what happened.

We took our dog to the emergency room after they had drained approximately two liters of fluid from his abdomen the previous day. That night, he started vomiting and was also very lethargic. The emergency veterinarian, Cristina Prieto, told us he was stable and administered methadone, as she informed us. When we got home, he was deeply sedated, to the point that we were very worried. We called the hospital twice, and both times they told us to wait for the effects to wear off, without recommending that we return for a follow-up evaluation. We weren't reassured and decided to return immediately. Our dog was admitted to the ICU with hypovolemic shock and, sadly, never left. Later, other veterinarians at the same hospital gave us different information about the medication administered, which left us with many unanswered questions that remain unanswered to this day.

When we go to a leading veterinary hospital, we expect to find professionals prepared to care for critically ill patients. However, over the weekend, with Lucía Molina in charge of the ICU, we were repeatedly told that we had to wait for Pablo to return from vacation. As owners, this made us extremely uneasy. Furthermore, it gave us the impression that some veterinarians in the ICU lacked the necessary experience to handle such complex cases. An intensive care unit requires highly experienced professionals who are confident in their decision-making, because the consequences can be irreversible.

I also want to report the actions of the veterinary assistant, Andrea Muñoz. Our dog could barely walk due to the inflammation caused by his liver disease, and in front of us, she handled him very roughly, pulling on his leash and trying to take him down some stairs instead of using the ramp. The handling was so rough that it dislodged one of the IV lines, causing it to bleed. Witnessing that was deeply painful and infuriating.

We also didn't understand the treatment we received from reception. After several days of diligently paying each bill for the hospital stay—which totaled well over four figures—they demanded payment for the day's visit in front of other clients before we could even speak to the veterinarian or see our dog. It was a completely inappropriate and unempathetic gesture.

I'm not going to judge the medical decisions, because I understand the enormous complexity of these kinds of cases. However, I do believe that something fundamental was missing: empathy and more honest communication with the family. We missed having someone clearly explain the true prognosis and when perhaps the most humane thing to do would be to stop prolonging the suffering. Sometimes, caring for an animal also means knowing when to let it rest.

Our animals are part of our family. When we go to a veterinary hospital, we're not just looking for medical expertise; we're also looking for compassion. Hopefully this review will help Veterios reflect on and improve those aspects that make the difference between a good hospital and a truly humane hospital.

Thank you for giving my little Bli a chance, thank you for the excellent care and love my little one received in his final days. Bli was a very special dog and we wanted to do everything we could for him, ensuring he received the best care, and we were absolutely right to choose you. Thank you so much for everything.

Thank you, Manuel, for your 5 stars! We're delighted to hear you had a positive experience at Veterios Referral Veterinary Hospital. ❤ We'd love to make your experience even better on your next visit. Is there anything you'd recommend we improve?

I took my cat to the clinic in very bad shape. She was extremely disoriented, barely eating, falling down, wandering around the house in cycles, and getting stuck in corners and nooks, not knowing how to get out or what to do. I took her to this clinic on the advice of my local veterinarian, and she was seen in veterinary neurology. The test results were terrible: a brain tumor, enormous as seen in the MRI scans, and slow-growing. The cat had been gradually deteriorating for many months, and now it was severely compressing her brain, causing her condition to worsen exponentially.

We spoke with a neurologist and a surgeon who told us that, despite the risks involved, a good recovery was very likely. They said they had performed the operation numerous times, and we went ahead with it, despite the high cost.

The result was magnificent. Four days after the operation, the improvement was noticeable as soon as we brought her home. After a week in which the cat was quite clumsy, lethargic, and sedated by the post-operative medication, once the dosage was reduced, she returned to her former self within another week—an incredible and complete recovery.

From being on the brink of imminent death, she practically rejuvenated. It's clear that months or years of mental confusion caused by the tumor have vanished, and she is more alert, active, and happy.

I went on a recommendation and it can only be described as a disappointment. One of the vets was very nice and coherent, but the other was very insistent that the drawer test was positive and that cruciate ligament surgery was necessary. Thank goodness I didn't take the dog there, and I won't again. The only thing that worries me is the €135 consultation fee.

BEFORE ANYONE GOES, PLEASE READ THIS REVIEW!! My dog ​​was admitted on Wednesday, November 12th. After charging us over €600, he stayed. I saw that he was getting worse every day, and every day there were new bills: €178, €80, €400 and some change, and the first one was almost €700. On Friday the 14th, I decided to discharge him voluntarily, mainly because I didn't see my dog ​​doing well there. I had to go back five hours later because he got worse at home that night, and it was the worst decision I could have made. My dog ​​almost died. They kept doing ultrasounds that showed he had worsened, yet they continued with the same useless treatment: IV fluids, probiotics, and a feeding tube. On Monday the 17th, I saw my dog ​​so sick, not eating and with no will to live, his paws all purple from the repeated injections they had given him in four days. I decided to discharge him again, as I preferred to risk watching him die while that team of "professionals" did nothing but take our money. I drove my dog ​​to our safe haven: Canservet, Boltaña Street. I will always be grateful to them. In two days, my dog ​​is a different dog; he's eating, playing... He spent two days on antibiotics that they refused to give him, despite my telling them he might need them. I will never set foot in this clinic again, even though the ophthalmologist used to work there. It was a nightmare having my dog ​​here. Every day of his hospitalization was uncertain because they didn't give you any information, and the lack of communication between the veterinarians themselves was obvious. Often, the afternoon shift couldn't even answer questions about the other shift, and vice versa. PLEASE DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE I DID OUT OF DESPERATION. LETTING THEM DIE HERE WHILE THEY "TRY TO CURE" THEM IS NOT HELPING OR SAVING OUR PET. THIS HOSPITAL SHOULD BE CLOSED.

I rescued a kitten I found in the street. It was only a few days old. I gave it special milk, and today it was a bit weak. It slept all day and didn't eat. I took it to the vet, who said it had milk in its lungs and wanted me to pay 500 euros, which I didn't have. I told them to put it up for adoption, and after two hours I called and they told me it had died when I brought it in. It didn't seem to be dying. I don't recommend going there; the doctors aren't very friendly if you don't speak their language.
I learned about them through our fantastic neurologist, Inés Ludeña, whose career change led us to Veterios. I loved them and highly recommend them.

Thank you so much, Ender, for your review! We're delighted to hear you were happy with our service after your visit.
We trust we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet.
Have a great day,
Veterinos Referral Veterinary Hospital

They are highly professional and always ready to operate, even on weekends, which is what you expect from a leading hospital. I've had to leave my dog ​​there several times, and I can go home with peace of mind knowing he's in the best hands.

Thank you so much, Jose, for your 4 stars!
We'd love to make your experience even better next time. Is there anything you'd recommend we improve?
Excellent service, they are super friendly and excellent professionals 👏 …

I am the owner of Bonzo, and we wanted to thank Dr. Andrea Molina for her professionalism, care, and compassion.

Thank you so much for making such a difficult time for us easier.

I came for the first time today. The professional and humane treatment was spectacular. I've never seen dogs, all of them, feel so calm. My little dog trusts the staff completely. They immediately establish a plan for diagnosis and treatment and ensure the animal's well-being. I have nothing but excellent things to say about this Veterinary Hospital. As someone else said here: thank you, thank you so much.

I returned today, May 6, 2026, years later, with my dog ​​Merlin. Both the assistant who did the triage and the veterinarian were efficient, excellent professionals, empathetic, and kind. Again, I can only say thank you. Five stars aren't enough!

I want to express my sincerest gratitude to the entire team at Veterios for the care my dog, Dexter, received during his hospitalization due to a pneumothorax caused by a foxtail.

This experience has also made us more aware of the dangers foxtails can pose to our dogs. We never imagined that something so seemingly insignificant could lead to such a serious situation and require such a major intervention.

From the very first moment, José, who was our primary veterinarian, conveyed professionalism, warmth, honesty, and trustworthiness. Along with him, Manuel, Jorge, and the rest of the team of veterinarians and staff at Veterios demonstrated extraordinary human and professional qualities.

The surgery was complex and very expensive, as it was necessary to remove part of Dexter's lung. Even so, we didn't hesitate for a second to give him the chance he deserved. Our 4-year-old Dex is part of our family, and seeing him recover day by day confirms that we made the right decision.

Thank you for your dedication, your respect, your love for Dexter, and for being with us during one of the most difficult times we've ever experienced. Today, Dex is improving, and we will continue to attend his checkups with the peace of mind that comes from knowing he's in the best hands.

To José, Manuel, Jorge, and the entire team: thank you from the bottom of our hearts for everything you've done for Dexter. Carol and Roberto

I don't recommend them. My vet referred me for a specific test that he couldn't perform at his clinic. They admitted my pet for 24 hours, running all sorts of tests (which were already done that same day and included in the report they provided). They didn't perform the requested test, and they lost 24 invaluable hours, which are vital in an emergency. I took my pet out of there and brought it to Puchol, and it was a completely different story.

These people are like the Vitaldent of veterinary clinics; they have their checklist of tests to perform, and everything else is irrelevant (including the opinions of the regular vet). And their prices are around two or three times higher in some cases compared to other hospitals. Obviously, they're free to charge whatever they want, but in a matter as delicate as the health of a living being, the disproportion is quite shocking. I felt that keeping track of costs was more important to them than helping a sick animal. Zero dedication.

I want to express my gratitude for the excellent care I received at this veterinary hospital. Alberto attended to me, and he was very kind, professional, and attentive at all times. He took the time to explain everything clearly and treated my pet with great care and affection. The experience was very positive, and he instilled a lot of confidence in me. I wholeheartedly recommend this veterinary hospital for the quality of its care and the compassionate treatment they provide. Thank you so much!

Thank you so much, Jose, for sharing your positive experience at Veterios Reference Veterinary Hospital! We are confident that we will continue to meet your expectations and those of your pet on your next visit.

I want to express my deepest gratitude to ophthalmologist David Pulido for all the care, dedication, and compassion he showed my cat from the very beginning.

I took her to him for a corneal sequestration that, unfortunately, was complicated by a very aggressive ulcer. Despite the complexity of the case, he did everything possible during the surgery to try and save her eye. Although it ultimately wasn't possible, I feel she was in the best hands.

Beyond his professionalism, I want to highlight how attentive he was at all times, his constant involvement, and the close support he showed us throughout the entire process. It's clear when someone truly loves their work and is involved not only as a veterinarian, but also with empathy and genuine care.

Thank you, David, for never giving up on her and for taking such good care of her.

In February, my 9-year-old dog was diagnosed with intestinal lymphoma. His clinic referred us to the oncology department at this hospital, and from the first day I met Sergio, the oncologist, I placed all my trust in him, and I wasn't wrong. It had been a very long time since I'd seen someone so professional and with such a kind heart. From the beginning, he was clear about the diagnosis and never influenced any of our decisions. He respected all our choices from day one, cared deeply for my dog, and gave us all the affection, love, and support we needed. I have no words to thank him enough for this entire process. I wish there were more professionals like him. On May 24th, Darko passed away, and although I know there's a very long process of grief and healing ahead, Sergio gave me the peace I needed to know that I did everything right for my baby. Thank you, Sergio, for being there for me during this time. I will always be grateful, and I know Darko would be too.

Terrible experience at Veterios. Our dog was very ill, and they constantly played with our hopes through exorbitant costs and endless tests, showing no sincerity or empathy. Charging €700 upfront just for taking our dog to their clinic says it all. It contrasts sharply with our experience at another hospital, both in terms of cost and professionalism. We came to this hospital because a veterinarian referred us. We hope their commission was worth it to compensate for such a lack of ethics and professionalism. If you're a novice like us, don't fall into this trap. If you've already visited this place, my condolences.

Our experience with Veterios veterinary hospital has been deeply disappointing. We took our 15-year-old dog in a delicate situation, seeking honesty, empathy, and professional guidance during a very difficult time for our family.

However, we felt that they prioritized performing expensive tests and procedures over providing a clear and realistic diagnosis. After consulting with other veterinary hospitals, the diagnosis was practically immediate, and they all agreed that the situation was obvious from the start.

The most painful part isn't just the money spent, but the feeling that they took advantage of the emotional vulnerability of a family worried about their pet. In moments like these, pet owners need transparency, humanity, and sincerity, not the feeling that every decision is geared toward increasing revenue.

I hope no one else has to go through a similar experience.
Poor animals, the way they make them suffer there in the yard, it's an alarming lack of empathy, sensitivity and direct care towards animals.

The service is a disgrace. They don't respect the neighbors' rest hours and couldn't care less when you ask them to please lower the noise. A total disgrace.

Today, April 30, 2026, I called to tell them that it's impossible to get any rest because of the use of the side patio for phone calls and for keeping some poor animals there suffering and making heartbreaking sounds 😢. Honestly, I don't know what they're doing to them, but poor animals. I called and the receptionist hung up on me. Great job, Veterios.
May 11, 10:00 am.
Go to the patio and see for yourself the noise level produced by the poor animals they keep suffering there so they don't bother you.
Should I start making videos to raise awareness?
The last time I went, I took my little one with a foxtail stuck in his ear. As always, the medical care and treatment were outstanding. I think they are great professionals.

At the end of February, we took our beloved Coco, a beautiful Basque Shepherd (Iletsua), to this hospital, referred by our regular veterinarian, as he was quite ill. In the end, on March 12th, we had to put him down. During his stay, all the staff who treated him, whose names we don't recall, were incredibly kind. We especially want to thank Pablo from internal medicine, who was the one we spoke with most, for his efforts in trying to cure Coco and his empathy towards us. Thank you so much, Pablo.

Although we are still grieving, it comforts us to know that Coco received the care he deserved in his final days.

Thank you, Rocio, for visiting Veterios Reference Veterinary Hospital and for your review!

We're delighted to hear your experience was positive 🥰
Have a great day!
A 24-hour clinic where the protocols are very inflexible and the prices are the complete opposite.

Today marks one month since our dog Roma had surgery for two herniated discs that suddenly left her paraplegic. We want to express our gratitude to the neurology and neurosurgery department at Veterios, especially to Natalia Acebes, who has been with us from the very beginning. We appreciate her professionalism, honesty, and excellent care, both with Roma and with us, her owners. Thanks to her expert advice, my little one walked out of the surgery, and a month later she's almost back to 100%. Thank you so much! ❤️

I want to leave this review solely about the administrative management and cost communication at Veterios. This is not a review of the veterinary care my dog ​​received. But be warned! I'm going to the Consumer Protection Office.

I went to the clinic with a previously sent written estimate for a neurological consultation and cytarabine administration—a treatment we've been receiving since 2023 at The Ralf Hospital in the UK. However, once there, and during the consultation, both the protocol and the costs communicated were confusing and, unfortunately, significantly higher than initially indicated.

After immediately stating that neither the protocol nor the amount matched the estimate and confirming that it was not feasible, the response was that I could go to another clinic if I wished. This clearly limited my ability to make a decision at that point, since the consultation (a three-figure fee) already had to be paid for when the final amounts were communicated, including items not previously explained.

Later, after complaining again when I went to pick up my dog, the center partially acknowledged the discrepancy and refunded part of the amount charged. However, they did charge a penalty.

After my initial complaint, I was offered a "reduced" quote—albeit higher than the one quoted in the email—for the follow-up appointment. They indicated it was an exceptional adjustment as a gesture of goodwill after "reviewing it with management." However, after my complaint, this quote was revised to a higher amount. In total, I received five quotes in eight hours.

During the consultation, I noted and pointed out the lack of preparation for the case. The previously sent clinical information had to be requested again; it wasn't integrated into the consultation. Upon leaving, it was necessary to reconfirm basic information about the protocol and medication my dog ​​was receiving, despite having been previously provided.

Meanwhile, during the day, the center gave me clinical documentation belonging to another patient. And again, their response to my concerns was to downplay it and suggest I go to another center.

Overall, the experience has been marked by inconsistent information, the absence of a clear follow-up protocol, and constant changes in costs, leading to a loss of trust and the need to change veterinary clinics and restart treatment at another hospital. These decisions will require me to pay for the initial consultation again at a different clinic to transfer the case.

On Sunday, May 3rd, I had to say goodbye to my beloved friend Cocoa, after almost 17 years together, due to age-related complications. I want to express my deepest gratitude for the warmth, professionalism, and empathy I received throughout the entire process. In particular, I thank Dr. Elena, who cared for her with great dedication from her arrival until her passing. I also thank the entire team of professionals at the hospital for their humane and respectful treatment during such a difficult time. Thank you so much for supporting us with such sensitivity.

Words cannot express our gratitude to the Veterios Referral Veterinary Hospital for everything they did for Oso and us during one of the worst moments of our lives.

We arrived at the emergency room after a very serious accident, with Oso suffering a very complicated open fracture in his leg, and from the very first second, they attended to us with absolutely impeccable speed, compassion, and professionalism. In a moment of immense fear and anxiety, knowing that your dog is in the hands of people who are truly committed and care makes a huge difference.

The entire team treated all three of us with incredible kindness, warmth, and empathy. They not only focused on saving and caring for Oso, but also on reassuring us and keeping us informed at all times. Furthermore, they tried to gather all possible prior medical information to give him the best possible care, demonstrating admirable dedication and professionalism.

Thanks to them, Oso was able to receive the urgent care he needed when he needed it most. We will always be deeply grateful for how they treated us and for the kindness, sensitivity, and care they showed our dog.

We wholeheartedly recommend this veterinary hospital. We wish all healthcare professionals, both human and veterinary, worked with the same dedication, empathy, and commitment they have here.
The service, both for pets and their owners, is exceptional. Highly professional.

My dog ​​had a CT scan over two weeks ago, but I didn't receive the results until 15 days later, even though I had to call repeatedly during that time to get them to send it. They finally sent it four days ago, without calling me or explaining anything at all, with incredibly technical conclusions indicating that my dog ​​has a serious condition. I called around 2 PM to ask for an explanation, and the receptionist told me she would notify the vet to call me back. They called me back more than two hours later to tell me that the vet would call me today, Monday (with a long weekend in between), as I was no longer there. I find it incredibly unprofessional and lacking in empathy, first the delay in giving me the results, then sending them without any explanation, and even after I called to request them, leaving without doing so.
I've been waiting for four days; they were supposed to call me back, but they still haven't. Will I have to call them again?

The facilities are truly spectacular, but they need to improve their customer service significantly.

What they did to our dog was inhumane. This place should be shut down. My dog ​​was admitted on Wednesday, May 29, 2026. He couldn't urinate, and it was practically an emergency. They hospitalized him and gave us a diagnosis that, to this day (because of everything that happened), I question. To begin with, the information or "medical report" was brief; it was just a matter of "waiting." During the 20-minute visits, we only saw a thirsty and hungry dog. Not to mention how purple his paws were. They said he wasn't eating, but with me, he ate everything and drank water desperately. Two days later, I insisted on getting his lab results, and they told me they didn't have them yet. So, what were they "treating" him on? But the worst happened later: I went to pick him up to take him home, and they told me they wouldn't release him to me with a catheter in place. I had already warned them the day before that I was taking him. The day I was supposed to pick him up, they called me at 11 a.m. to tell me that "he removed the catheter himself in the early morning," even with the protective cover on his head. The dog had an obstruction and hadn't had the catheter since the early morning. When my dog ​​arrived, he hadn't urinated at all (imagine how many hours it had been since he'd gone). We were scared and decided to leave him alone for another day so they could insert the catheter, since it was a holiday and no one was available. It was then that I asked directly what was happening, and I was informed that he hadn't eaten since being admitted. The response was that he "didn't want to eat," and that kidney patients and those who are sedated often have a poor appetite or nausea, but his reaction clearly indicated hunger.

Throughout the entire process, we received no information. We weren't given a clear diagnosis or a realistic treatment plan, and we were even told that a cat in his condition couldn't have any quality of life, which completely contradicts how he was before the sedations.

After 36 hours of hospitalization and fluid therapy, his kidney function didn't improve, while his overall condition visibly worsened after the successive sedations. He became extremely thin, disoriented, and weak.

Furthermore, upon discharge, only pain medication was prescribed, even though the clinical report itself stated that pain could not be assessed because the animal was sedated. Initially, no medication was prescribed for nausea, nor was any food intake stimulant provided, which is especially concerning for a kidney patient in his condition. The nausea medication had to be requested later from our veterinarian, as I didn't receive a response from them until the following day.

The feeling was one of a lack of attention to our concerns and a prioritization of unnecessary protocols over the individual well-being of the animal.

Ultimately, we requested voluntary discharge because we felt that the hospitalization was doing more harm than good, and that was indeed the case. I don't know how much longer he will stay, as he is still in terrible shape and continues to show signs of sedation. He was a cat who was incredibly active, ate perfectly, and had a very good quality of life.
